definition_zh: 令人不快的；不舒服的；不客气的；使人为难的
definition_en: not enjoyable or comfortable, or rude and unfriendly
core_image: 刚端起汤碗就闻到一股馊味
scene: 公交车在雨天挤得满当当，有人把滴着水的伞搁在别人裤脚上。 The damp smell made the ride distinctly unpleasant.
sceneCN: 这里 unpleasant 是「令人不快的」（第 1 个义项：让人不舒服、不愉快）；句意为潮湿的气味让这趟车程明显令人难受。端起汤碗闻到馊味的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「令人不快地；不客气地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愉快；不快之事」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「令人愉快的」
同源动词，义为「使高兴；取悦」

senses.title: Something that is not enjoyable to the senses
senses.definition: not enjoyable to see, hear, smell, or touch
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉、听觉、嗅觉或触觉上让人难受
senses.example: There was an unpleasant smell from the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 下水道里冒出一股难闻的气味。
senses.why: The prefix means not and the base means pleasing, so the word starts as simply the negative of pleasant.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「令人愉快的」，因此这个词起初就是 pleasant 的反面。

senses.title: Something bad that arrives without warning
senses.definition: used of news, surprises, or events that one would rather not have
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们宁可不发生的消息、意外或事件
senses.example: The test results came as an unpleasant surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 检验结果成了一个不愉快的意外。
senses.why: Anything that spoils pleasure is unpleasant, and bad news spoils it in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把愉悦一扫而空的东西就是令人不快的，坏消息正是一下子把它扫空。

senses.title: A person who is rude or hard to deal with
senses.definition: used of a person whose manner is rude or unkind
senses.definitionCN: 形容说话行事无礼、刻薄的人
senses.example: The clerk was unpleasant to the old man at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台后的店员对那位老人很不客气。
senses.why: A person's manner of displeasing others is named by the same adjective that names the experience.
senses.whyCN: 一个人让别人不痛快的那种态度，也用同一个形容词来命名。

senses.title: A task or duty that one dreads
senses.definition: used of work that is boring, dirty, or upsetting
senses.definitionCN: 形容无聊、肮脏或令人难受的工作
senses.example: Cleaning the drains is an unpleasant task nobody volunteers for.
senses.exampleCN: 清理下水道是件没人主动愿意干的烦人活。
senses.why: Duty has no smell, yet it can be felt as the same sourness in the nose from the core image.
senses.whyCN: 职责本身没有气味，但做起来时鼻子里的那股酸味是一样的。

senses.title: An awkward situation that embarrasses people
senses.definition: used of situations that make those involved feel awkward
senses.definitionCN: 形容让在场的人都感到尴尬的处境
senses.example: Asking about the money put her in an unpleasant position.
senses.exampleCN: 问起那笔钱让她陷入很为难的处境。
senses.why: When an external thing causes inner discomfort, the discomfort moves into the situation itself.
senses.whyCN: 当外物带出内心不适时，这种不适就转移到了处境本身。

intro.en: Another plain negative compound, this time over an adjective that descends from Latin placere, to please.
intro.cn: 又一个朴素的否定复合词，这次压在源自拉丁语 placere（使高兴）的形容词之上。

items.en: The native prefix un- is added to borrowings to reverse their meaning.
items.cn: 本土前缀 un- 被加到借词上以反转其词义。

items.en: Placere meant to please or to be acceptable, with the adjective placidus, calm and pleasing.
items.cn: placere 意为「取悦、被接受」，形容词 placidus 意为「平和的、可喜的」。

items.en: Plaire brought the verb into French, and the present participle plaisant meant pleasing.
items.cn: plaire 把这个动词带入法语，现在分词 plaisant 意为「令人愉快的」。

items.en: Pleasant enters English from the French participle and describes what gives pleasure.
items.cn: pleasant 由这个法语分词进入英语，用来形容给人愉快的事物。

items.en: Unpleasant is formed by the negative prefix and extends from smells to people and duties.
items.cn: unpleasant 由否定前缀构成，并从气味扩展到人物与职责。

items.en: Its noun unpleasantness later becomes a polite word for a quarrel or an awkward scene.
items.cn: 其名词形式 unpleasantness 后来成为争吵或尴尬场面的委婉说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the please family, and the near-meaning group collects words for what we dislike.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 please 词族展开，近义组汇集表示令人嫌恶的词。

normalIntro.en: Everything about the word is familiar: an everyday negative prefix over the ordinary word for pleasure.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的一切都很熟悉：日常的否定前缀压在日常表示愉悦的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus pleasant: the negative is taken directly from the positive.
normal.cn: un- 加 pleasant：否定直接取自肯定形式。

normal.en: An unpleasant smell and an unpleasant surprise cover the two most common collocations.
normal.cn: an unpleasant smell 与 an unpleasant surprise 覆盖了最常见的两类搭配。

normal.en: The adverb unpleasantly is used mainly of weather, sounds, and smells.
normal.cn: 副词 unpleasantly 主要用于天气、声音和气味。

normal.en: The noun unpleasantness often means a quarrel rather than a feeling.
normal.cn: 名词 unpleasantness 常指一场争执，而不是一种感受。

normal.en: Pleasant, please, and pleasure share the Latin root placere.
normal.cn: pleasant、please、pleasure 共享拉丁词根 placere。

abstract.en: Smell soup that has stood too long in a warm kitchen.
abstract.cn: 闻一碗在热厨房里放久了的汤。

abstract.en: Sit beside a passenger whose wet umbrella drips on your shoe.
abstract.cn: 坐在一位湿伞往你鞋上滴水的乘客旁边。

abstract.en: Watch a room go quiet after someone asks the wrong question.
abstract.cn: 看一个房间在有人问错问题之后安静下来。

examples.en: An unpleasant smell came from the rubbish bin behind the kitchen.
examples.cn: 厨房后面的垃圾桶里冒出一股难闻的气味。

examples.en: He was asked to stay calm even when the customer was unpleasant to him.
examples.cn: 即使顾客对他很不客气，他也被要求保持冷静。

examples.en: Cleaning the cellar is an unpleasant task, but somebody must do it.
examples.cn: 清理地窖是件烦人的活，但总得有人干。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不累死」——被派去干又脏又烦的活儿，嘴上说着俺不累死，心里早就不痛快了。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ pleasant（令人愉快的），pleasant 源自拉丁语 placere（使高兴）经古法语 plaisant 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One sourness in the senses spreads to news, people, duties, and the awkward scenes those create.
sensesIntro.cn: 感官里的一股酸味，进而扩展到消息、人物、差事，以及这些带出的尴尬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smell at the nose that spoils the appetite.
core.cn: 核心意象：扑到鼻子里、把胃口赶跑的一股气味。

branches.en: The sensory branch: what offends smell, ear, or eye.
branches.cn: 感官分支：冲撞嗅觉、听觉或视觉之物。

branches.en: The news branch: the surprise nobody wanted.
branches.cn: 消息分支：谁都不想收到的意外。

branches.en: The person branch: manner that makes others wince.
branches.cn: 人物分支：让别人皱眉的态度。

branches.en: The duty branch: work that is dirty or dull.
branches.cn: 职责分支：又脏又闷的工作。

branches.en: The situation branch: a scene that leaves everyone stuck.
branches.cn: 处境分支：让所有人都僵住的一幕。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over a French adjective that goes back to a Latin verb of pleasing.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在经由法语借入、可追溯至拉丁「取悦」动词的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is placere, to please, with placidus and the noun placitum behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族以 placere（使高兴）为核心，其后有 placidus 与名词 placitum。

items.exampleCN: 这部电影让孩子们很高兴。

items.example: Pleasant comes from the French participle.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 我们度过了一个愉快的夜晚。

items.example: The room smelled unpleasantly of smoke.
items.exampleCN: 房间里有一股难闻的烟味。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 约定之事；令人满意之事

definition_zh: 移民；外来移民
definition_en: a person who comes to live permanently in another country
core_image: 机场到达大厅里推着行李车、手里攥着旧护照的人
scene: 清晨的到达厅灯还没全亮，已经有几家人聚在出口旁边。 Many immigrants arrived that week, and volunteers handed out water and city maps.
sceneCN: 这里 immigrant 是「移民」（第 1 个义项：移入另一国定居的人），句意是那一周许多移民抵达，志愿者分发水和城市地图。画面里有到达大厅、行李车和旧护照。

senses.title: A person who moves in to settle
senses.definition: someone who leaves one country to live permanently in another
senses.definitionCN: 离开一国、到另一国长期定居的人
senses.example: Her grandparents were immigrants from Ireland.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母是来自爱尔兰的移民。
senses.why: The prefix in- marks moving inward, so the word looks at the newcomer from the side of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 标示「向内移动」，因此这个词是从抵达地的视角看新来者。

senses.title: A member of a growing community
senses.definition: used collectively for groups whose labour and families reshape a city
senses.definitionCN: 集合使用，指以劳动与家庭改变一座城市的人群
senses.example: Immigrants opened most of the shops on that street.
senses.exampleCN: 那条街上的多数店铺都是移民开的。
senses.why: News and policy talk of immigrants in groups, so the singular noun often stands for a social category.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与政策常成组谈论移民，于是这个单数名词常代表一个社会类别。

senses.title: Frequently paired with a status word
senses.definition: used with words such as illegal or skilled to describe legal position or training
senses.definitionCN: 与 illegal、skilled 等词连用，说明法律身份或技能
senses.example: Skilled immigrants filled the vacant jobs quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 技术移民很快填补了空缺岗位。
senses.why: Because immigration is regulated, the word habitually takes a second word marking where a person stands in law.
senses.whyCN: 由于移入受管控，这个词习惯性地带一个说明法律身份的第二词。

intro.en: Immigrant is built from a Latin verb for moving into a place, and it was coined in English quite late.
intro.cn: immigrant 由拉丁语「迁入」动词构成，在英语里出现得相当晚。

items.en: Migrare meant to move from one place to another, whether a person or a bird.
items.cn: 拉丁语 migrare 意为从一处迁往另一处，人和鸟都可用。

items.en: Immigrare added the direction inward, the arrival into a new land.
items.cn: 加上表示向内的前缀后，immigrare 指迁入新的地方。

items.en: The participle immigrans named a person in the act of moving in.
items.cn: 分词 immigrans 指正在迁入的一个人。

items.en: English coined immigrant in the late eighteenth century, when migration was beginning to be counted and debated.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末造出 immigrant，当时人口迁徙刚开始被统计与争论。

items.en: The word spread through newspapers and census tables, always tilting towards the receiving country.
items.cn: 这个词通过报纸与人口普查表传播，始终倾向接收国的视角。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the migr- family; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who move.
note.cn: 形近组收 migr- 迁徙词根家族；近义组收表示迁移者的词。

entries.definition: One who leaves a country, the out- version of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国的人，是本词的「向外」版。

entries.definition: The process or policy side of the same movement.
entries.definitionCN: 同一迁徙过程或政策层面。

entries.definition: A mover without the in- prefix, often for work or season.
entries.definitionCN: 不带 in- 前缀的迁徙者，常指为工作或季节迁徙。

entries.definition: Anyone newly arrived, with no legal sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 新到的人，完全无法律含义。

entries.definition: One who takes land and stays, often in a colonial context.
entries.definitionCN: 占地定居者，多用于殖民语境。

entries.definition: One who flees danger, a distinct legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 逃离危险者，属一种独立的法定身份。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the in- and ex- pair, the migr- root, and the arrival hall image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用上 in- 与 ex- 的对立、migr- 词根，以及到达大厅的画面。

normal.en: Im-migr-ant: move in, versus e-migr-ant: move out.
normal.cn: im-migr-ant 是移入，e-migr-ant 是移出。

normal.en: The root migr- is the same one in migrate and migration, the act of moving.
normal.cn: 词根 migr- 也见于 migrate 与 migration，即迁移这一动作。

normal.en: Three beats, stress the first: IM-mi-grant.
normal.cn: 三个拍子，重音在前：IM-mi-grant。

normal.en: -ant marks a person, like servant and applicant.
normal.cn: -ant 标示人，如 servant 与 applicant。

normal.en: Immigrant and emigrant describe one traveller twice: leaving there, arriving here.
normal.cn: immigrant 与 emigrant 是同一个旅人的两面：从那边离开，到这边抵达。

abstract.en: The word depends on point of view: the same journey makes a person an emigrant on one coast and an immigrant on the other.
abstract.cn: 这个词取决于视角：同一趟旅程，在一岸是移出者，在另一岸是移入者。

abstract.en: Behind every statistic stands a bag with too few clothes and a name that others still struggle to say.
abstract.cn: 每个统计数字背后都站着一个行李装得太薄的人，和一个别人还念不准的名字。

abstract.en: A country measures immigration in numbers, but lives it in kitchens and classrooms.
abstract.cn: 国家用数字衡量移民，却在厨房与教室里经历它。

examples.en: The city grew quickly because immigrants kept arriving.
examples.cn: 移民不断到来，这座城市迅速扩张。

examples.en: Many immigrant families keep two languages at home.
examples.cn: 许多移民家庭在家里保留两种语言。

examples.en: He came to Britain as an immigrant in the 1970s.
examples.cn: 他在上世纪七十年代作为移民来到英国。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + migr 迁移 + ant 人——迁进来定居的人，即移民

root: 拉丁语 migrare「迁移」加向内前缀 in- 成 immigrare「迁入」，分词 immigrans，英语十八世纪末造 immigrant。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an individual settler, a social group, and a status-qualified category.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：移入定居的个人、作为社会群体的移民，以及带身份限定的类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a luggage trolley and an old passport in a half-lit arrivals hall.
core.cn: 核心意象：半亮的到达大厅里，行李车与一本旧护照。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: one family moving in and staying.
branches.cn: 个人线：一家人迁入并留下来。

branches.en: THE GROUP LINE: whole streets change shape with them.
branches.cn: 群体线：整条街的面貌因他们而变。

branches.en: THE STATUS LINE: skilled, illegal, recent qualify the word.
branches.cn: 身份线：skilled、illegal、recent 都在限定这个词。

branches.en: THE CENSUS LINE: governments count them for policy.
branches.cn: 普查线：政府为他们统计以定政策。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: immigrant often appears before families and workers.
branches.cn: 家庭线：这个词常出现在 families 与 workers 之前。

intro.en: Immigrant is a prefix, a Latin root and the person-marking -ant, with a full directional family.
intro.cn: immigrant 是前缀、拉丁词根与标示人的 -ant 的组合，周围有一套方向对立词。

latinIntro.en: Migrare and imm-igrare are attested in Latin, so the direction of the prefix is well founded.
latinIntro.cn: migrare 与 immigrare 在拉丁语中均有文献，前缀的方向有据可依。

items.example: Import uses the same inward prefix.
items.exampleCN: import 用同一个向内前缀。

items.meaning: to move from place to place
items.exampleCN: 候鸟每年秋天向南迁徙。

items.example: Servant and assistant follow this pattern.
items.exampleCN: servant 与 assistant 都属此类。
一位移民开了那家面包店。

items.meaning: to move in as a settler
the process or policy of moving in
items.example: Immigration is a national debate here.
items.exampleCN: 移民事宜在这里是全国性议题。

items.example: Emigrants left by the same port.
items.exampleCN: 移居国外的人也从同一个港口离开。

definition_zh: 搬运工；行李员；医院勤杂工；门房；看门人；黑啤酒
definition_en: a person paid to carry luggage, a hospital worker who moves patients and equipment, a doorkeeper or caretaker, or a dark beer
core_image: 车站月台上，一个穿制服的人把两只旧皮箱一前一后提在手里
scene: 深夜的旅馆门口，雨还在下，一个穿制服的人接过旅客手里的两只大箱子。 The porter carried both suitcases up the narrow stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 porter 是「搬运工、行李员」（第 1 个义项：替人搬运行李的人）；句意为行李员把两只箱子搬上窄楼梯。图中可辨识物件：旅馆门口、雨、大箱子、制服。

pos.zh: 搬运工；行李员；医院勤杂工；门房；看门人；黑啤酒

derivatives.zh: 由 porter 加 -age 构成，义为「搬运；搬运费」
由 porter 与 house 复合，原指兼卖黑啤酒的餐馆，后指一种厚切牛排
由 porter 加 -ess 构成，义为「女门房；女搬运工」

senses.title: A person paid to carry luggage
senses.definition: a person whose job is to carry bags and luggage for travellers, especially at a station or hotel
senses.definitionCN: 以替旅客搬运行李为职业的人，尤指在车站或旅馆工作的人
senses.example: The porter carried both suitcases up the narrow stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 行李员把两只箱子搬上窄楼梯。
senses.why: Latin portare means to carry and -er names the person who does it; the first sense is simply the carrying job.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，-er 指做这件事的人；第一个义项就是这份搬运的工作。

senses.title: A hospital worker who moves patients
senses.definition: a hospital worker who moves patients, beds, samples or equipment between wards
senses.definitionCN: 在医院各病房之间运送病人、病床、样本或设备的勤杂人员
senses.example: A porter wheeled her down to the X-ray department.
senses.exampleCN: 一名勤杂工用轮椅把她推到放射科。
senses.why: Hospitals borrowed the carrying word for the staff who move people and equipment, because the job is still transport inside a building.
senses.whyCN: 医院借用了这个「搬运」词来称运送人与设备的员工，因为这份工作仍是在楼内做运输。

senses.title: A doorkeeper or caretaker
senses.definition: a person who guards the entrance of a building, especially a college or a block of flats, and often looks after it
senses.definitionCN: 看守建筑物入口的人，尤指学院或公寓楼的看门人，往往还兼管杂务
senses.example: The porter at the college gate checked our names before letting us in.
senses.exampleCN: 学院门口的门房先核对了我们的名字才放行。
senses.why: This sense has a different Latin source: porta means gate, and portarius was the gatekeeper, so one English spelling carries two histories.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项另有拉丁来源：porta 意为门，portarius 是守门人；所以同一个英语拼写背着两段历史。

senses.title: A dark, strong beer
senses.definition: a dark brown beer made with roasted malt, originally associated with London market porters
senses.definitionCN: 用烘烤麦芽酿成的深褐色啤酒，最初与伦敦市场的搬运工有关
senses.example: He ordered a pint of porter and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一品脱黑啤酒，坐到窗边。
senses.why: The drink was shortened from porter's ale, the beer sold to market porters, so the job name became the name of what they drank.
senses.whyCN: 这种酒由 porter's ale 缩略而来，本是卖给市场搬运工的啤酒；于是职业名变成了他们所喝之物的名字。

intro.en: Porter is two Latin words that fell into one English spelling: portare, to carry, and porta, a gate, each with its own Old French descendant.
intro.cn: porter 是两个拉丁词落进同一个英语拼写：portare（搬运）与 porta（门），各自带着自己的古法语后裔。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, and with the agent suffix -arius it gave portarius, a carrier.
items.cn: portare 意为搬运，加上表示施动者的后缀 -arius，就得到 portarius（搬运者）。

items.en: Porta meant a gate or door; the same -arius made portarius a gatekeeper, so the two jobs shared a Latin shape.
items.cn: porta 意为大门、出入口；同一个 -arius 又造出表示守门人的 portarius，两种职业在拉丁语里形状相同。

items.en: Old French carried the two words onward as porteo(u)r, a carrier, and portier, a doorkeeper.
items.cn: 古法语把这两个词分别传成 porteo(u)r（搬运者）与 portier（守门人）。

items.en: Middle English spelled both as porter, so the carrier and the gatekeeper became one form in English.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者都写作 porter，搬运者与守门人由此在英语里合成一个形式。

items.en: Porter beer is short for porter's ale, named for the market porters who drank it; the drink sense is the newest branch.
items.cn: porter 啤酒是 porter's ale 的缩略，得名于喝这种酒的市场搬运工；酒这一义项是最晚长出的分支。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same carrying root and the harbor word; the near-meaning group gathers people who carry or guard entrances.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「搬运」词根上的形式以及表示港口的词；近义组收搬运东西或看守入口的人。

entries.definition: The work of carrying goods, or the charge for it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 porter 加 -age 构成，义为「搬运工作；搬运费」。

entries.definition: Able to be carried, built on the same Latin verb portare.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一拉丁动词 portare 构成，义为「便携的」。

entries.definition: A harbor or an opening; the harbor word comes from Latin portus, not from the carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但表示港口的 port 来自拉丁 portus，不是搬运词根。

entries.definition: To bring goods into a country, built on portare with the prefix in-.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-（进入）加 portare（搬运）构成，义为「进口」。

entries.definition: A person or company that carries goods or people.
entries.definitionCN: 搬运者；承运人；强调承担运输的人或公司。

entries.definition: A person who carries something, especially in a formal role.
entries.definitionCN: 持送者；强调正式地拿着或递送某物的人。

entries.definition: A person employed to guard the entrance of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 门童；门卫；强调守在门口的人。

entries.definition: A hotel employee who helps guests with luggage, bookings and local information.
entries.definitionCN: 旅馆礼宾员；除行李外还替客人安排事务。

normalIntro.en: The word has two Latin roots, carrying and gatekeeping, and its family keeps returning to loads, entrances and the people who handle them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词有两条拉丁根，一条是搬运，一条是守门；同族词反复回到货物、入口以及照管它们的人。

normal.en: Porter the carrier is portare plus -er, the person who carries.
normal.cn: 表示搬运工的 porter 是 portare 加 -er，即「搬运的人」。

normal.en: Porter the doorkeeper is porta plus -arius, the person at the gate; the two Latin words became one English spelling.
normal.cn: 表示门房的 porter 是 porta 加 -arius，即「守在门口的人」；两个拉丁词在英语里拼成了同一个样子。

normal.en: Old French porteur meant carrier and portier meant doorkeeper, and English merged them both into porter.
normal.cn: 古法语 porteur 指搬运者，portier 指守门人，英语把两者都并进了 porter。

normal.en: Porter beer was shortened from porter's ale, the dark beer sold to London market porters.
normal.cn: porter 啤酒由 porter's ale 缩略而来，是卖给伦敦市场搬运工的深色啤酒。

normal.en: A hospital porter still carries people rather than bags, which shows how far the carrying sense can stretch.
normal.cn: 医院勤杂工搬的是人而不是行李，可见「搬运」这一义项能伸到多远。

abstract.en: Two jobs share one spelling because a gate and a load both sit at the edge of a journey.
abstract.cn: 两种职业共用一个拼写，因为门与行李都处在旅程的边缘。

abstract.en: A porter stands where arrival becomes entry: he takes the bag or checks the name before the guest goes in.
abstract.cn: 门房站在「到达」变成「进入」的地方：他接过箱子，或先核对名字，客人才能进去。

abstract.en: The beer kept the name of the workers who drank it, which is how a job can outlive itself in a glass.
abstract.cn: 这种酒留下了喝它的工人的名字，一份职业就这样在杯子里延续下来。

examples.en: The porter carried both suitcases up the narrow stairs.
examples.cn: 行李员把两只箱子搬上窄楼梯。

examples.en: A porter wheeled her down to the X-ray department.
examples.cn: 一名勤杂工用轮椅把她推到放射科。

examples.en: He ordered a pint of porter and sat by the window.
examples.cn: 他点了一品脱黑啤酒，坐到窗边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡特」——在坡道上替人提箱子的人；porter 就是搬运工，也是门房。

root: porter 有两条拉丁来路：一条是 portare（搬运）加 -er，指搬运工、行李员；另一条是 porta（门）加 -arius，指门房、看门人。两词在英语里拼成同一个样子。黑啤酒 porter 则由 porter's ale 缩略而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is someone who handles what passes through a threshold; the senses divide into carrying luggage, moving patients, guarding a gate, and the beer named after carriers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是照管通过某道门槛之物的人；义项由此分出搬行李、运病人、守大门，以及以搬运工命名的啤酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a uniformed figure on a station platform holding two old suitcases, one in each hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站月台上，一个穿制服的人一前一后提着两只旧皮箱。

branches.en: a bag lifted from a taxi to a hotel desk
branches.cn: 行李从出租车提到旅馆前台

branches.en: a wheelchair pushed along a hospital corridor
branches.cn: 轮椅沿医院走廊被推着

branches.en: a name checked at a college gate
branches.cn: 学院门口核对的姓名

branches.en: a dark pint set down on a pub table
branches.cn: 一杯深色啤酒放到酒馆桌上

branches.en: a uniformed worker standing where people arrive and ask for help
branches.cn: 穿制服的人站在人们到达并求助的地方

intro.en: The word joins a carrying verb and a gate noun to two agent suffixes, and the same pieces also build porterage and the compound porterhouse.
intro.cn: 这个词把「搬运」动词与「门」名词分别接到两个施动后缀上，同样的部件还造出了 porterage 与复合词 porterhouse。

latinIntro.en: Porter comes from two Latin nouns of agency: portarius, a carrier from portare, and portarius, a gatekeeper from porta; Old French kept them apart before English merged the spellings.
latinIntro.cn: porter 来自两个表示施动者的拉丁名词：由 portare 来的「搬运者」，与由 porta 来的「守门人」；古法语还分得清，英语却把拼写合并了。

items.meaning: the work or charge of carrying

definition_zh: 卸货；卸下；退出子弹；倾诉（心事）；卸载（数据）
definition_en: to remove goods from a vehicle, to take bullets out of a gun, or to tell someone your worries
core_image: 卡车后挡板放下，几个工人把一箱箱货搬下来，车厢一点点变轻变空
scene: 货车在仓库门口倒车停稳，司机跳下来掀开帆布，晨光里全是灰尘。 They began to unload the boxes at six in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 unload 是「卸货、卸下」（第 1 个义项：把货物从车船上搬走）；句意为他们早上六点开始卸箱子。车厢一点点被搬空的那种变轻感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 倾诉；把心里的负担说出来

collocations.zh: 向某人倾诉；把情绪发泄到某人身上

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「卸货；卸载」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「未装货的；未装弹的」
本词去掉 un-，义为「装载；装填」
由 load 加 -er 构成，义为「装卸工；装载机」

senses.title: Take goods off
senses.definition: to remove goods or cargo from a ship, truck, or other carrier
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从船、卡车等运输工具上搬下来
senses.example: The crew unloaded the fish onto the wet harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们把鱼卸到湿漉漉的码头石板上。
senses.why: Un- reverses and load is what was put on board: the cargo comes off, and the ship rides higher.
senses.whyCN: un- 表示反向，load 是被装上的东西：货物离船，船身也随之抬高。

senses.title: Take the bullets out
senses.definition: to remove the ammunition from a gun so that it cannot fire
senses.definitionCN: 把弹药从枪里取出，使枪不能击发
senses.example: He unloaded the rifle before handing it to the guide.
senses.exampleCN: 他把步枪里的子弹退出来，才交给向导。
senses.why: A gun is loaded like a cart, so the same verb empties it and makes it safe to pass on.
senses.whyCN: 枪和车一样会被「装上」东西，因此同一个动词让它变空、变得可以递出去。

senses.title: Put down a burden
senses.definition: to set down something heavy that one has been carrying
senses.definitionCN: 把一直扛着的重物放下来
senses.example: The porters unloaded their baskets at the top of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 搬运工在台阶顶上把筐放下。
senses.why: Here the carrier is a person, and the load is carried on the back rather than in a vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 这里的载具是人，负载扛在背上而不是装在车里。

senses.title: Tell someone your worries
senses.titleCN: 倾诉；把心里的话说出来
senses.definition: in informal speech, to tell someone all your problems or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中，把烦恼或感受全部说给别人听
senses.example: She called her sister to unload after the long meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开完那个长会，她打电话给姐姐倾诉了一番。
senses.why: Trouble behaves like freight: once it is set down on someone else, the speaker feels lighter.
senses.whyCN: 烦恼像货物一样：一旦放到别人那边，说话的人就轻了。

senses.title: Remove from a system
senses.definition: of data or software, to transfer it out or remove it from a place
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或程序，把它们转移出去或从某处移除
senses.example: The app unloads the photos to save space on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用把照片卸载出去，以节省手机空间。
senses.why: A phone or a server is the new warehouse, and its files are the freight to be moved out.
senses.whyCN: 手机或服务器成了新的仓库，里面的文件就是待搬出的货。

intro.en: Unload is the native negative prefix on load, a word that English took from the same Germanic root as lade.
intro.cn: unload 是本土否定前缀加 load，load 与 lade 同出日耳曼语词根，为英语所继承。

items.en: The verb hladan meant to draw water or to pile up goods, and gave the modern lade and load.
items.cn: 古英语动词 hladan 意为「舀水、堆货」，演变为现代的 lade 与 load。

items.en: The noun lode, meaning a load or a course, and the verb laden kept the sense of piling a burden on.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 lode 意为「负载、路线」，动词 laden 保留了「堆积重负」之意。

items.en: Un- was added to make unload, to take the burden off again, and the word covered ships, carts and guns.
items.cn: 加上 un- 构成 unload，表示把重负重新取下，用于船、车与枪。

items.en: Railways and lorries made unloading a daily industrial routine, with dockside cranes named for it.
items.cn: 铁路与卡车让卸货成为日常的工业工序，码头的吊机也以它命名。

items.en: Computers and counselling both borrowed the image: data and worries can now be unloaded too.
items.cn: 计算机与心理咨询都借用了这个意象：数据与心事如今也能「卸」出去。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and load forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of removing, emptying, or confessing.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 load 一族的词；近义组收表示移走、清空或倾诉的动词。

entries.definition: To put goods or ammunition on; the word without the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装载」，即去掉前缀的词。

entries.definition: Adjective for a vehicle or gun with nothing in it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未装货的、未装弹的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the work of taking a load off.
To send data from a computer to a server; the opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上传」，方向相反。

entries.definition: To bring data from a network onto a device.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「下载」，从网络取到设备上。

entries.definition: To make a container have nothing in it; the result rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倒空」，强调结果。

entries.definition: To unload cargo formally, or to release a person; used in shipping and law.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸货、释放」，多用于航运与法律。

entries.definition: To relieve oneself of a worry by telling someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸下负担、倾诉」，偏书面。

entries.definition: To tell a secret to someone you trust; quieter than unload.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吐露」，比 unload 更安静、更私密。

entries.definition: A general verb for taking something away from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「移走」，泛称从某处拿走东西。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus load structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 load 的朴素结构，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and load is the burden: unload is to take the burden off.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，load 是重负：unload 就是把重负取下。

normal.en: A truck is unloaded at the dock; a gun is unloaded before it is handed over.
normal.cn: 卡车在码头卸货；枪在交出之前要退出子弹。

normal.en: Upload and download move data; unload moves it out of the way.
normal.cn: upload 与 download 是搬数据；unload 是把数据挪走。

normal.en: To unload on someone can mean to tell them your troubles, or to blame them.
normal.cn: unload on someone 既可指向人倾诉，也可指把气撒到人身上。

normal.en: Unloaded and empty are close, but unload is the act.
normal.cn: unloaded 与 empty 意思接近，但 unload 是动作。

abstract.en: Picture a cart that gets lighter with every box: the word tracks the moment weight leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车每卸一箱就轻一点：这个词跟着重量离开的那一瞬间。

abstract.en: From boxes to bullets to worries, unload always means the same: take the charge out.
abstract.cn: 从货物到子弹再到心事，unload 始终是同一个意思：把「装进去的东西」拿出来。

abstract.en: A person who unloads a burden is the same image, only the cargo cannot be seen.
abstract.cn: 倾诉的人用的是同一个意象，只是货物看不见。

examples.en: Workers unloaded the truck in less than an hour.
examples.cn: 工人们不到一小时就把卡车卸完了。

examples.en: Always unload the gun before cleaning it.
examples.cn: 清洁枪支前一定要先退出子弹。

examples.en: She unloaded her worries onto her friend over dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭时她把心里的烦恼全向朋友倾诉了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的楼德」——安把楼上堆的货物一件件搬下来：卸货

root: 由否定前缀 un- 加 load（源自古英语 hladan「舀水、堆货」，与 lade 同源）构成，字面即「把装上的东西取下」；近代从船只、车辆、枪械扩展到数据与心事的「卸载」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unload all remove a charge that had been put in: goods, bullets, a heavy basket, pent-up worries, or data.
sensesIntro.cn: unload 的五个义项都在把先前装进去的东西拿出来：货物、子弹、重筐、憋着的心事，或数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the tailgate drops and boxes are carried out of the truck.
core.cn: 核心意象：后挡板放下，箱子一箱箱被搬出车厢。

branches.en: THE CARGO: goods leave the ship, truck or plane.
branches.cn: 货物线：货物离开船、卡车或飞机。

branches.en: THE AMMUNITION: bullets leave the gun so it is safe.
branches.cn: 弹药线：子弹离开枪膛，枪才安全。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: a carried basket is set down at the top of the steps.
branches.cn: 重负线：扛着的筐在台阶顶上被放下。

branches.en: THE FEELINGS: what was held inside is said out loud.
branches.cn: 情感线：憋在里面的东西被说出口。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: data is moved out to free space.
branches.cn: 系统线：数据被移出去以腾出空间。

intro.en: Unload is native on both sides: an English prefix on an English verb, with English suffixes on top.
intro.cn: unload 两边都是本土成分：英语前缀加英语动词，上面再加英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin core here; the Latin-based cousins appear only as formal near meanings.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语核心；拉丁语来源的近义词只作为正式说法列出。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「装载」倒过来。

items.example: The root names the charge being carried.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被装上的负载。
它把 load 变成 loader。

items.example: An older noun from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根上较早的名词。

items.example: The formal synonym from Latin carricare.
items.exampleCN: 源自拉丁语 carricare 的正式近义词。

definition_zh: 彩虹；七彩排列；虚幻的希望
definition_en: an arch of colours seen in the sky when sunlight passes through rain; a similar arrangement of colours; an illusory hope that is chased but never reached
core_image: 雨后山脊上方一道弯弯的彩弧
scene: 雨后云层裂开，山脊上方出现一道弯弯的彩弧。 A rainbow arched over the wet fields after the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 rainbow 是「彩虹」（第 1 个义项：阳光穿过雨滴时天空出现的彩色弧形）；句意为暴风雨过后，一道彩虹横跨湿漉漉的田野。画面里可留意：裂开的云层、弯曲的彩弧、发亮的水面。

pos.zh: 彩虹；七彩排列；虚幻的希望

collocations.zh: 在彩虹之上（比喻美好远方）

derivatives.zh: rainbow 与 coloured 复合，指彩虹色的、五颜六色的
rainbow 加 -like，指像彩虹一样的
rainbow 与 trout 复合，指虹鳟这种鱼

senses.title: An arch of colours in the sky
senses.definition: a curved band of colours seen when sunlight enters drops of rain
senses.definitionCN: 阳光进入雨滴时天空中出现的一条彩色弧带
senses.example: A rainbow appeared over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山丘上方出现了一道彩虹。
senses.why: The word is simply rain joined to bow, because the coloured band is shaped like a bent bow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 rain 与 bow 的结合，因为那条彩带形状像一张弯弓。

senses.title: An arrangement of colours
senses.definition: a set of colours arranged in the same order as a rainbow
senses.definitionCN: 按彩虹相同次序排列的一组颜色
senses.example: The scarf was a rainbow of stripes.
senses.exampleCN: 那条围巾是彩虹般的条纹。
senses.why: Once the arch became a familiar symbol of ordered colour, anything arranged in that order could be called a rainbow.
senses.whyCN: 这条彩弧既成了有序颜色的熟悉象征，任何按此顺序排列的东西都可称为 rainbow。

senses.title: An illusory hope
senses.definition: a hope or goal that looks beautiful but cannot be reached, as in chasing rainbows
senses.definitionCN: 一个看似美好却无法达到的希望或目标，如 chase rainbows
senses.example: He spent his life chasing rainbows.
senses.exampleCN: 他一生都在追逐虚幻的希望。
senses.why: A rainbow is bright and real yet untouchable, and that image became a way of naming hopes that vanish as you approach them.
senses.whyCN: 彩虹明亮而真实，却无法触及，这一意象便成了命名「越靠近越消失的希望」的方式。

intro.en: Rainbow is a native English compound of rain and bow, recorded in Old English as a word for the coloured arch.
intro.cn: rainbow 是 rain 与 bow 的英语本族复合词，古英语中已有表示这条彩色拱弧的词。

items.en: Regnbuga joined regn, rain, to buga, a bow, naming the arch by its shape.
items.cn: regnbuga 把表示雨的 regn 与表示弓的 buga 结合，按形状命名这条拱弧。

items.en: Bow named both a weapon and any curved thing, so the sky's arch looked like a bow laid across the clouds.
items.cn: bow 既指武器，也指任何弯曲之物，因此天空的拱弧看起来像一张横在云上的弓。

items.en: Middle English kept the compound and gradually reshaped the spelling toward the modern form.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个复合词，并逐步把拼写改成现代形式。

items.en: The rainbow became a symbol of promise and of ordered colour, which produced the sense of a colour arrangement.
items.cn: 彩虹成了许诺与有序颜色的象征，由此生出「颜色排列」这一义项。

items.en: Modern English uses rainbow for the arch, for colour patterns and for hopes that cannot be grasped.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rainbow 指拱弧、颜色图案，以及无法抓住的希望。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and words for curved shapes; the near-meaning group gathers words for colour bands.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与表示弯曲形状的词；近义组收表示色带的词。

entries.definition: Water falling from clouds.
A curved weapon or a curved shape.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的武器或弯曲的形状。

entries.definition: A fish with a coloured stripe along its side.
entries.definitionCN: 体侧有一条彩色纹带的鱼。

entries.definition: Having many bright colours.
A curved line or shape.
The band of colours produced when light is separated.
entries.definitionCN: 光被分解时形成的一条色带。

entries.definition: A glass shape that separates light into colours.
entries.definitionCN: 把光分解成各种颜色的玻璃体。

entries.definition: The visible hues of light or objects.

normalIntro.en: The word is a rain bow, an arch of colour shaped like a bent weapon; from that arch come the colour pattern and the hopeless hope.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是「雨中的弓」，一条形状像弯弓的彩弧；由这条弧生出颜色图案与虚幻希望两层意思。

normal.en: Rainbow is rain plus bow, because the arch looks like a bow laid across the sky.
normal.cn: rainbow 是 rain 加 bow，因为这条拱弧看起来像横在天上的一张弓。

normal.en: A rainbow appears only when sunlight and rain meet, which is why it vanishes so quickly.
normal.cn: 彩虹只在阳光与雨相遇时出现，所以消失得那么快。

normal.en: Rainbow colours always come in the same order, from red at the top to violet at the bottom.
normal.cn: 彩虹的颜色总按同样顺序排列，上端是红，下端是紫。

normal.en: Chasing rainbows means pursuing something beautiful that you can never actually reach.
normal.cn: chasing rainbows 意为追逐某种美丽却永远无法真正触及的东西。

normal.en: Rainbow trout is named for the coloured band along its flank, not for the sky.
normal.cn: rainbow trout 因体侧的彩色纹带而得名，而不是因为天空。

abstract.en: A rainbow exists only from where you stand, which makes it a useful image for hopes that are real and unreachable at once.
abstract.cn: 彩虹只从你所站的位置才成立，这使它成为「既真实又不可触及之希望」的绝佳意象。

abstract.en: The colours are ordered, yet no two people see the same arc, and both facts are true together.
abstract.cn: 颜色是有序的，但没有两个人看见同一条弧，两件事同时为真。

abstract.en: Something made only of light and water can still promise land, and that is the whole power of the image.
abstract.cn: 只由光与水构成的东西仍能许诺土地，这正是这一意象的全部力量。

examples.en: A faint rainbow stood over the harbour after the shower.
examples.cn: 阵雨过后，港口上方挂着一道淡淡的彩虹。

examples.en: The children's paintings formed a rainbow on the wall.
examples.cn: 孩子们画作在墙上排成了一道彩虹。

examples.en: She warned him that chasing rainbows would cost him years.
examples.cn: 她警告他，追逐虚幻的希望会让他付出许多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞恩波」——雨后在天空弯成一张弓的彩波，记住 rainbow 是彩虹。

root: 古英语 regnboga（reg 雨 + buga 弓）→ 中古英语 rainbow → 现代英语 rainbow；同族有 rain、bow、rainbow trout。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rain-made bow; the senses divide into the arch itself, any rainbow-ordered colours, and a hope that cannot be grasped.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「由雨形成的弓」；义项分为拱弧本身、任何按彩虹次序排列的颜色，以及无法抓住的希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved band of colours above a ridge after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后山脊上方一道弯曲的彩带。

branches.en: an arch over wet fields
branches.cn: 横在湿田野上的一道弧

branches.en: a scarf striped in seven hues
branches.cn: 七种颜色条纹的围巾

branches.en: a road that keeps moving away
branches.cn: 不断远去的路

branches.en: the sky's band and a copy of it in cloth
branches.cn: 天上的色带与布上对它的模仿

branches.en: ordered colours and an unruly hope
branches.cn: 有序的颜色与难以驯服的希望

intro.en: The word is a native compound, so its parts are two English nouns and the endings and compounds built on them.
intro.cn: 这个词是本族复合词，其成分是两个英语名词，以及在此基础上构成的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 系紧；扣住；固定；集中（注意力）
definition_en: to close or tie something firmly, to attach it in place, or to fix attention on something
core_image: 登机前，乘客低头把安全带扣紧，听见清脆的咔哒声
scene: 起飞前，她系好了安全带。 She fastened her seat belt before takeoff.
sceneCN: 这里 fasten 是「系紧」（第 1 个义项）；句意：起飞前，她系好了安全带。

senses.title: To close or tie securely
senses.definition: to close or join something firmly
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢地关闭或连接某物
senses.example: Please fasten your seat belt.
senses.exampleCN: 请系好安全带。
senses.why: The core sense is making something secure.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是使某物牢固。

senses.title: To attach firmly
senses.definition: to fix something in place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物固定在某个位置
senses.example: He fastened the shelf to the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他把架子固定在墙上。
senses.why: The sense extends from closing to attaching objects.
senses.whyCN: 词义从关闭延伸到固定物件。

senses.title: To fix attention on
senses.definition: to direct your eyes or attention firmly at something
senses.definitionCN: 把目光或注意力牢牢投向某物
senses.example: Her eyes fastened on the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的目光紧紧盯在屏幕上。
senses.why: Attention is treated as something tied down.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被当作可以被系住的东西。

intro.en: Fasten comes from Old English fæstnian, to make firm, from fæst, firm.
intro.cn: fasten 源自古英语 fæstnian（使牢固），来自 fæst（牢固的）。

items.en: Fæst meant firm or fixed.
items.cn: fæst 意为牢固或固定。

items.en: Fæstnian meant to make something firm.
items.cn: fæstnian 意为使某物牢固。

items.en: Fasten meant to secure or tie something.
items.cn: fasten 意为固定或系住某物。

items.en: The word extended to buttons, doors, and ropes.
items.cn: 该词扩展到纽扣、门和绳索。

items.en: Fasten now means to close, attach, or fix.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fasten 意为关闭、附着或固定。

note.en: Fasten is compared with similar-looking verbs and with verbs for joining.
note.cn: 把 fasten 与形近动词以及表示连接的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to make something happen sooner
to make an animal fat
a device that closes something
to fasten with string or rope
to make something safe and firm
to join one thing to another

normalIntro.en: Fast plus the verb ending en gives fasten, to make firm.
normalIntro.cn: fast 加动词结尾 en 构成 fasten，意为使牢固。

normal.en: Fast plus en makes a verb meaning to make firm.
normal.cn: fast 加 en 构成表示「使牢固」的动词。

normal.en: A fastener fastens things together.
normal.cn: fastener 把东西扣在一起。

normal.en: Unfasten means to undo.
normal.cn: unfasten 意为解开。

normal.en: Fasten your seat belt is a common instruction.
normal.cn: 系好安全带是常见提示语。

normal.en: Fasten on means to grip or focus on.
normal.cn: fasten on 意为抓住或集中于。

abstract.en: The verb turns firmness into an action.
abstract.cn: 这个动词把「牢固」变成一种动作。

abstract.en: Attention can be fastened like a buckle.
abstract.cn: 注意力也可以像带扣一样被系住。

abstract.en: To fasten is to create a fixed point in a moving world.
abstract.cn: 系紧就是在变动世界里创造一个固定点。

examples.en: She fastened the gate with a chain.
examples.cn: 她用链条把大门拴紧。

examples.en: The dress fastens at the back.
examples.cn: 这条裙子在背后扣合。

examples.en: He fastened the papers together with a clip.
examples.cn: 他用夹子把文件夹在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: fast 是「牢固的」，加动词后缀 en 构成 fasten，表示「使牢固、系紧」。

root: 源自古英语 fæstnian（使牢固），由 fæst（牢固的）加动词后缀构成。

sensesIntro.en: Fasten means to close or tie something, to attach it firmly, or to fix attention on it.
sensesIntro.cn: fasten 意为系紧扣住、牢固附着，或把注意力集中在某处。

core.en: Making something firmly fixed or closed.
core.cn: 使某物牢牢固定或闭合。

branches.en: Closing a belt, button, or door.
branches.cn: 扣好带子、纽扣或门。

branches.en: Attaching an object to a surface.
branches.cn: 把物体固定到某个表面。

branches.en: Directing the eyes or mind at one point.
branches.cn: 把目光或心思投向一点。

branches.en: Both senses involve making a firm connection.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及建立牢固连接。

branches.en: Objects and attention can both be fixed.
branches.cn: 物体与注意力都可以被固定。

intro.en: Fasten forms nouns for devices and verbs for undoing.
intro.cn: fasten 构成表示扣件的名词与表示解开的动词。

latinIntro.en: Old English fæstnian is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 fæstnian 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: a device or act of fixing

items.example: The zipper is a common fastener.
The shop sells buttons and fasteners.
The dog fastened on the bone.

definition_zh: 徒劳的；无效的；自负的；爱虚荣的
definition_en: producing no result despite effort, or too proud of one's own appearance or abilities
core_image: 对着已经干了的水井一遍遍摇动辘轳
scene: 井底早已见底，绳子放下去只碰到干泥，他还是摇了一遍又一遍，桶提上来时依旧空空。 All their efforts to save the old tree were in vain.
sceneCN: 这里 vain 是「徒劳的、无效的」（第 1 个义项：白费力气而没有结果）；句意为他们挽救那棵老树的努力全白费了。对着干井摇辘轳的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「虚荣；虚妄」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「徒劳地；自负地」
复合名词，义为「自负；虚夸的荣耀」

senses.title: Producing no result
senses.definition: of an effort or attempt that brings no result
senses.definitionCN: 形容努力或尝试毫无结果
senses.example: Their attempts to find the missing dog were vain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们寻找丢失小狗的尝试都白费了。
senses.why: The Latin adjective vanus means empty, so an effort that leaves nothing behind is literally an empty one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词 vanus 意为「空的」，因此毫无结果可言的努力，字面上就是「空」的。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase in vain
senses.definition: used in the phrase in vain, meaning without success
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in vain，表示没有成功
senses.example: We waited in vain for a bus that never came.
senses.exampleCN: 我们白等了一班始终没来的公交。
senses.why: The phrase in vain keeps the old sense of emptiness and is now the commonest way to use the word.
senses.whyCN: in vain 这个短语保留着古老的「空」义，如今也是用这个词最常见的说法。

senses.title: Too proud of one's looks or abilities
senses.definition: too pleased with one's own appearance, talents, or achievements
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的外貌、才能或成就过于得意
senses.example: He is vain about his handwriting and shows it to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的字很自负，见人就展示。
senses.why: Pride needs something to stand on, and when there is nothing inside, the word calls that pride empty too.
senses.whyCN: 自负本需要某种依托，而内里什么都没有时，这个词就同样把这份傲慢说成空的。

senses.title: Empty of substance, without basis
senses.definition: lacking any real substance or ground
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质内容或根据
senses.example: The promise of easy money was a vain hope.
senses.exampleCN: 那种轻松赚钱的许诺只是虚妄的希望。
senses.why: The original Latin sense of emptiness survives most plainly here: a hope with nothing inside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「空」的本义在这里保留得最直白：一只里面空无一物的希望。

intro.en: From Latin vanus, empty, through French; the same root lies behind vanish and vanity.
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 vanus（空的），经法语进入英语；同一词根还藏在 vanish 与 vanity 里。

items.en: Vanus meant empty, hollow, or without effect, and vanitas named emptiness.
items.cn: vanus 意为空的、虚的、无效的，vanitas 指空虚。

items.en: Vain entered French with the sense of empty or useless, with vanité beside it.
items.cn: vain 以「空的、无用的」之义进入法语，vanité 并行使用。

items.en: English adopts the word in the fourteenth century, and in vain becomes a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪采用这个词，in vain 成为固定短语。

items.en: The sense of conceited grows from the idea of having nothing inside but thinking one has much.
items.cn: 「自负」这层意思从「内里空无一物却自以为很多」这一想法长出来。

items.en: Vainly doubles as adverb of both effort and pride.
items.cn: vainly 同时充当「徒劳」与「自负」两义的副词。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the van- family of emptiness, and the near-meaning group sets futile apart from proud.
note.cn: 形近组展示表示「空」的 van- 词族，近义组则把徒劳与自负分开。

entries.definition: excessive pride in oneself
without success
to disappear completely
a blood vessel, only the sound is close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 血管；只是读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: useless and without result
having no purpose
too proud of oneself
not boastful about oneself

normalIntro.en: Remember the empty Latin base: an empty effort fails, and an empty person fills the gap with pride.
normalIntro.cn: 记住拉丁词基的「空」：空的努力白费，空的人则用自负来填补。

normal.en: In vain is far more common than any other use of the adjective.
normal.cn: in vain 比这个形容词的其他用法常见得多。

normal.en: A vain attempt and a vain hope both mean an empty one.
normal.cn: vain attempt 与 vain hope 都指落空的。

normal.en: The noun is vanity, not vainness.
normal.cn: 名词是 vanity，而不是 vainness。

normal.en: Take someone's name in vain means to speak of them lightly.
normal.cn: take someone's name in vain 指轻慢地提某人的名字。

normal.en: Vainly covers both senses: tried vainly, smiled vainly.
normal.cn: vainly 兼两义：tried vainly 与 smiled vainly。

abstract.en: Picture turning a well handle over a dry well.
abstract.cn: 想象对着干井一遍遍摇辘轳。

abstract.en: See a bucket come up with only cracked mud in it.
abstract.cn: 看桶提上来只有干裂的泥。

abstract.en: Watch someone admire their own reflection in a shop window.
abstract.cn: 看有人对着橱窗欣赏自己的影子。

examples.en: They searched in vain for the lost key.
examples.cn: 他们白找了半天那把丢失的钥匙。

examples.en: His vain attempt to please everyone satisfied nobody.
examples.cn: 他想讨好所有人的徒劳尝试谁也没取悦。

examples.en: She was too vain to wear her old coat in public.
examples.cn: 她太爱虚荣，不肯穿着旧外套出门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂恩」——对着空气喂了一声恩，什么回应也没有，全白费。

root: 拉丁语 vanus（空的、无效的）与 vanitas（空虚），经古法语 vain 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The core of emptiness gives effort without result, the fixed phrase in vain, empty hopes, and finally pride that fills an empty self.
sensesIntro.cn: 「空」这个核心先给出没有结果的努力，再给出固定说法 in vain，再给出空洞的希望，最后是填补空虚自我的自负。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket drawn from a dry well.
core.cn: 核心意象：从干井里提上来的空桶。

branches.en: The effort branch: work that leaves nothing behind.
branches.cn: 努力分支：干完什么也没留下。

branches.en: The phrase branch: waiting without success.
branches.cn: 短语分支：空等而没有结果。

branches.en: The pride branch: an empty self filled with praise.
branches.cn: 自负分支：空虚的自我用赞叹填满。

branches.en: The hope branch: a promise with nothing inside it.
branches.cn: 希望分支：里面空无一物的许诺。

branches.en: The base branch: emptiness itself, plainest in Latin.
branches.cn: 词基分支：最朴素的就是「空」本身。

intro.en: A French-shaped adjective from a Latin base of emptiness; English adds only -ly and the noun vanity.
intro.cn: 一个来自拉丁「空」词基、经法语成形的形容词；英语只在其上加 -ly，并另有名词 vanity。

latinIntro.en: Latin vanus meant empty or vain, and vanitas named vanity; the root van- also gives vanish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vanus 意为空的、虚的，vanitas 指虚荣；词根 van- 还给出 vanish。

items.exampleCN: 词根 van- 承载「空」义。

items.example: Vanish turns the same root into an action.
items.exampleCN: vanish 把同一词根变成动作。

items.example: In vain is a whole idiom.
items.exampleCN: in vain 是完整的习语。
modest 回应了「自负」那一义。

definition_zh: 强迫；迫使；使不得不
definition_en: to force someone to do something, or to make something happen inevitably
core_image: 一只手按在背上，把人往前推了一步
scene: 暴雨越下越大，司机只好把车停到路边。 The storm compelled them to stop and wait.
sceneCN: 这里 compel 指「迫使」（第 1 个义项：让人不得不做）；句意是暴雨迫使他们停下来等。

derivatives.zh: 令人信服的；引人入胜的

senses.title: To force a person
senses.definition: to make someone do something by force or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用力量或压力使某人做某事
senses.example: Illness compelled her to leave the job.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病迫使她辞去工作。
senses.why: The Latin base means to drive, so the word carries a push from behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为驱赶，所以这个词带有从背后推的力量。

senses.title: To make something unavoidable
senses.definition: to make an event or feeling impossible to avoid
senses.definitionCN: 使某件事或某种感受无法避免
senses.example: The story compels attention from the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事从第一行就让人不得不注意。
senses.why: Pressure can fall on things as well as people, and then compel means to demand.
senses.whyCN: 压力也会落在事物上，此时 compel 意为强烈要求。

intro.en: Compel comes from Latin compellere, to drive together, from com, together, and pellere, to push.
intro.cn: compel 来自拉丁语 compellere，意为往一处赶，由 com（一起）与 pellere（推动）构成。

items.en: Pellere meant to push, to drive or to strike.
items.cn: pellere 意为推、赶或击打。

items.en: Compellere meant to drive someone into a corner.
items.cn: compellere 意为把人逼到角落。

items.en: Roman law used it for forcing a person to appear.
items.cn: 罗马法律用它表示强制某人到场。

items.en: Old French compeller kept the sense of pressure.
items.cn: 古法语 compeller 保留了压力的含义。

items.en: English compel widened to any strong necessity.
items.cn: 英语 compel 扩展到任何强烈的必然。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short verbs close in shape to compel, and the meaning group ranks the verbs of pressure from force to urging.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compel 形状相近的短动词，近义组按从强迫到敦促排出表示压力的动词。

entries.definition: to try to win against others
very convincing or interesting
to gather material into one work
to make someone do something
to make it necessary for someone
to push someone strongly to act

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand on the back, then move to pressure on events and to the demand that wins attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从背上的那只手开始，再走到落在事情上的压力以及赢得注意的强烈要求。

normal.en: Com- is together and pel means push, so compel is a push that leaves no room.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pel 是推，compel 就是推到没有退路。

normal.en: Be compelled to is the passive shape of having no choice.
normal.cn: be compelled to 就是没有选择时的被动说法。

normal.en: A compelling story does not force you, yet you cannot look away.
normal.cn: 引人入胜的故事不强迫你，你却移不开眼。

normal.en: Compulsion is the inner version of an outer push.
normal.cn: compulsion 是外在推力在心里的版本。

normal.en: Compel takes an object and a to-clause: compel someone to act.
normal.cn: compel 后面接宾语和不定式：迫使某人行动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flat on a back, moving a person one step.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平按在背上，把人推前一步。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pressing forward at a narrow door.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在窄门前向前挤。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet pulling a needle across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象磁铁把针吸过桌面。

examples.en: Heavy snow compelled the airport to close.
examples.cn: 大雪迫使机场关闭。

examples.en: Poverty compelled many families to move.
examples.cn: 贫困迫使许多家庭搬迁。

examples.en: Her courage compels respect.
examples.cn: 她的勇气令人敬佩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compel 记成 com（一起）加 pel（推）：一起往前推，就是迫使。

root: 源自拉丁语 compellere，com- 表示一起，pellere 表示推动，本义是往前赶，后引申为强迫与使不得不。

sensesIntro.en: From pushing a person, to pressing an event upon you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从推着人走，到把某件事压到你面前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed on a back, pushing a person one step forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在背上，把人往前推了一步。

branches.en: A person under pressure is the oldest scene for this word.
branches.cn: 被压力压住的人，是这个词最古老的场景。

branches.en: Events and feelings can press just as hard as people.
branches.cn: 事件与感受也能像人一样用力压迫。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a force the other side cannot refuse.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在对方无法拒绝的力量上。

branches.en: The passive voice, be compelled, keeps the whole weight intact.
branches.cn: 被动形式 be compelled 把那份重量完整保留下来。

branches.en: What compels attention holds it without asking.
branches.cn: 能抓住注意力的东西，不必征求就抓住了。

intro.en: Compel is built on Latin com, together, plus pellere, to push.
intro.cn: compel 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 pellere（推动）构成。

latinIntro.en: The pushing base also appears in expel, repel and propel.
latinIntro.cn: 表示推动的词基也出现在 expel、repel 与 propel 里。

items.example: They were compelled to leave early.

items.meaningCN: 令人信服的；引人入胜的

items.meaning: in a way that holds attention
items.example: The film tells the story compellingly.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影把故事讲得引人入胜。

items.meaning: a strong urge or the act of forcing
items.example: He felt a compulsion to check the door.
items.exampleCN: 他有一种非去查看门不可的冲动。

items.example: She has a compulsive need to tidy.
items.exampleCN: 她有一种强迫性的整理需求。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be stopped
items.exampleCN: 他不由自主地反复看手机。

items.example: The course is compulsory for first years.
items.exampleCN: 这门课对一年级学生是必修的。

definition_zh: 执行；强制实施；迫使服从
definition_en: to make people obey a law or rule, often by using authority
core_image: 交警站在路口，确保每辆车都遵守信号灯
scene: 警察负责执行交通规则。 The police enforce traffic rules.
sceneCN: 这里 enforce 是「执行」（第 1 个义项：用权威确保人们遵守规则）；句意：警察负责执行交通规则。

senses.title: To make a law or rule obeyed
senses.definition: to make sure that a law or rule is obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 确保法律或规则被遵守
senses.example: The police enforce traffic rules.
senses.exampleCN: 警察负责执行交通规则。
senses.why: The prefix en- adds force, so the word means putting force behind a rule so it is not merely written.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 加上力量，因此这个词意为给规则加力，使它不只是写在纸上。

senses.title: To force people to accept something
senses.definition: to make people accept or follow something by authority or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过权威或压力使人们接受或遵守某事
senses.example: The school enforces a strict dress code.
senses.exampleCN: 学校强制执行严格的着装规定。
senses.why: Enforcement can involve pressure, so the word also covers forcing compliance.
senses.whyCN: 执行可能涉及压力，因此这个词也涵盖强迫服从。

senses.title: To give strength to a claim or rule
senses.definition: to make an argument, right, or condition stronger or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 使论点、权利或条件更有力、更有效
senses.example: The new evidence enforces their claim.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据使他们的主张更有力。
senses.why: To enforce is to add force, so a claim can be strengthened as a rule can be upheld.
senses.whyCN: enforce 就是加力，因此主张能像规则一样被加强。

intro.en: Enforce comes from Old French enforcier, to give force to something.
intro.cn: enforce 来自古法语 enforcier，意为给某物加力。

items.en: Fortis means strong, the root behind force.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮，是 force 背后的词根。

items.en: Enforcier means to strengthen or compel.
items.cn: enforcier 意为加强或强迫。

items.en: English borrows enforce with the sense of giving force.
items.cn: 英语借入 enforce，表示施加力量。

items.en: The legal sense of carrying out laws becomes common.
items.cn: 在近代早期，执行法律的义项变得常见。

items.en: Enforce now chiefly means making rules obeyed.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enforce 主要指使规则被遵守。

note.en: Enforce makes rules obeyed; implement puts plans into action, and impose forces something on people.
note.cn: enforce 使规则被遵守，implement 把计划付诸行动，impose 把某物强加于人。

normalIntro.en: Enforce means to put force behind a rule so people must follow it.
normalIntro.cn: enforce 意为给规则加力，使人们必须遵守。

normal.en: Police enforce the law.
normal.cn: 警察执行法律。

normal.en: The school enforces a dress code.
normal.cn: 学校执行着装规定。

normal.en: Strictly enforce the ban.
normal.cn: 严格执行禁令。

normal.en: Enforcement keeps rules alive.
normal.cn: 执行让规则保持生命力。

normal.en: Enforce shares a root with force.
normal.cn: enforce 与 force 共享词根。

abstract.en: Picture a referee's whistle stopping play.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判的哨声停止比赛。

abstract.en: See a red light obeyed by every car.
abstract.cn: 想象每辆车都遵守红灯。

abstract.en: Think of a rule written on a wall and acted on.
abstract.cn: 想象写在墙上并被执行的规定。

examples.en: The police enforce traffic rules.
examples.cn: 警察负责执行交通规则。

examples.en: The school enforces a strict dress code.
examples.cn: 学校强制执行严格的着装规定。

examples.en: The new evidence enforces their claim.
examples.cn: 新证据使他们的主张更有力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因福斯」——把力量加进去，让规定真正生效；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 enforcier（加力），来自拉丁语 fortis（强壮）。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers carrying out laws, forcing compliance, and giving strength to a claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖执行法律、强迫服从，以及加强主张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red light obeyed by every car.
core.cn: 核心意象：每辆车都遵守的红灯。

branches.en: The base sense is making a law obeyed.
branches.cn: 基本义是使法律被遵守。

branches.en: Authority can also force acceptance of a rule.
branches.cn: 权威也能迫使人们接受规定。

branches.en: The same force can strengthen a claim.
branches.cn: 同样的力量也能加强主张。

branches.en: Law and pressure both aim at compliance.
branches.cn: 法律与压力都以服从为目标。

branches.en: Putting force behind words gives them effect.
branches.cn: 给言语加力使其产生效果。

intro.en: Enforce is en- plus force: to put force into a rule.
intro.cn: enforce 是 en- 加 force：把力量放进规则。

latinIntro.en: Force comes from Latin fortis, strong, through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: force 经古法语来自拉丁语 fortis（强壮）。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 加上力量。

items.example: Force is the heart of enforce.
items.exampleCN: force 是 enforce 的核心。
enforcing 标记正在进行的动作。

items.example: Enforce the law is a common phrase.
items.exampleCN: enforce the law 是常见搭配。

definition_zh: 导航；航行；确定位置并找到路线的过程，也指网页或系统的导览结构
definition_en: the process of finding a position and a route, the act of sailing, or the menu structure that guides users through a site
core_image: 船在无岸的海上凭星位与海图校正方向，一步步靠近港口
scene: 浓雾里看不见岸，船长靠罗盘方位和灯塔的间隔校正航向，慢慢贴近港口。 With no shore in sight, the captain corrects the course by compass bearing and the spacing of lighthouses, a patient art of navigation.
sceneCN: 这里 navigation 指「确定位置并找到航线的过程」（第 2 个义项：靠方位与地标不断校正）；句意为浓雾中看不见岸，船长凭罗盘与灯塔间距修正航向，慢慢驶近港口。图中可辨识物件：罗盘、海图、灯塔、雾中的船首；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 航行；导航；导览结构（不可数）

senses.title: Sailing on water
senses.definition: the act of sailing or steering a vessel along a route
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶船只沿航线行驶的行为
senses.example: Navigation on the river began before roads were built.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路还没有修好之前，河上航行就已开始。
senses.why: navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive' is literally ship-driving, so the oldest sense is the movement of a hull through water.
senses.whyCN: navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」，字面就是「驾船」；最古老的含义正是船体在水上的移动。

senses.title: Position fixing and route finding
senses.definition: the process of determining where one is and which course leads to the destination
senses.definitionCN: 确定自己在哪里、哪条航线通向目的地的过程
senses.example: The captain corrected the course by compass and lighthouses.
senses.exampleCN: 船长凭罗盘与灯塔校正了航向。
senses.why: the core of navigation is two questions, where am I and where next; every instrument serves one of them.
senses.whyCN: 导航的核心是两个问题：我在哪里、下一步往哪；每件仪器都在为其中之一服务。

senses.title: Website navigation
senses.definition: the menus, links and layout that let a user move through a site or app
senses.definitionCN: 让用户在网站或应用中移动的菜单、链接与布局
senses.example: Clear navigation kept visitors from leaving the site.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的导航让访客没有离开网站。
senses.why: a user is also a traveller: the menu is a chart of the site, and a bad chart produces the digital equivalent of being lost.
senses.whyCN: 用户也是行者：菜单是网站的海图，海图糟糕就会产生数字版的迷路。

senses.title: Animal navigation
senses.definition: the ability of animals to orient and travel toward a goal over long distances
senses.definitionCN: 动物辨向并长距离前往目标的能力
senses.example: Monarch butterflies manage navigation across a continent.
senses.exampleCN: 帝王蝶能完成跨大陆的导航。
senses.why: biology uses the word because the same two questions apply without instruments: where am I, and which way is home.
senses.whyCN: 生物学使用这个词，因为同样两个问题在没有仪器时也成立：我在哪，家在哪边。

senses.title: Air and space navigation
senses.definition: plotting and correcting a course through the air or in orbit
senses.definitionCN: 在空中或轨道上规划并修正航线
senses.example: Space navigation relies on signals from ground stations.
senses.exampleCN: 航天导航依赖地面站信号。
senses.why: as the medium changes, the instruments change, but the loop of fix, compare and correct remains.
senses.whyCN: 介质改变，仪器随之改变，但「定位、比对、修正」的循环不变。

senses.title: Navigation technology
senses.definition: the instruments and systems that support positioning and routing
senses.definitionCN: 支持定位与选路的仪器与系统
senses.example: The app's navigation depends on four satellites.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的导航依赖四颗卫星。
senses.why: metonymy lets the activity name its tools, so navigation can mean the equipment that makes it possible.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让活动命名其工具，因此 navigation 也可以指使活动得以进行的设备。

senses.title: Inland waterway transport
senses.definition: the movement of goods or people on rivers and canals
senses.definitionCN: 在河流与运河上运送货物或人员
senses.example: Inland navigation carries coal along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 内河航运沿运河运送煤炭。
senses.why: the commercial sense narrows the old sailing sense to a transport mode counted in tonnage.
senses.whyCN: 商业义把古老的航行义收窄为一种以吨位计量的运输方式。

senses.title: The science or skill of navigating
senses.definition: the body of knowledge and technique required to find and follow a route
senses.definitionCN: 寻找并沿路线行进所需的知识与技术总体
senses.example: Navigation was taught as a mathematical art.
senses.exampleCN: 导航曾被当作一门数学技艺来教授。
senses.why: a practice that can be taught becomes a discipline, and the noun shifts from doing to knowing how.
senses.whyCN: 可以教授的实践会成为一门学问，名词便从「做」转向「知道怎么做」。

intro.en: Navigation comes from Latin navigatio, from navigare 'to sail', itself navis 'ship' plus agere 'to drive'. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: navigation 来自拉丁 navigatio，源自动词 navigare「航行」，而 navigare 由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Navis meant 'ship, boat'; it belongs to an old Indo-European word for a vessel and survives in navy and in naval.
items.cn: navis 意为「船、舟」；它属于古老的印欧语「船」词，留在 navy 与 naval 中。

items.en: Agere meant 'to drive, lead, do'; it is the verb behind agent, act and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为「驾驶、引领、做」；它是 agent、act 与 agenda 背后的动词。

items.en: Navis plus agere produced navigare, 'to sail, steer a ship'; the compound is literal, not metaphorical.
items.cn: navis 加 agere 构成 navigare「航行、驾船」；这个复合是字面的，不是比喻。

items.en: The noun navigatio 'a sailing, a voyage' supplied the English word through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 navigatio「航行、航程」在 16 世纪经法语提供英语词形。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word extended to animal orientation and to the menus that guide users through software, both treating travel as a path toward a goal.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到动物辨向，以及引导用户使用软件的菜单；两者都把行进当作通往目标的路径。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation is not exactly fixed, and the pre-Indo-European origin of navis is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；navis 在印欧语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same navis plus agere family; group two holds related travel and guidance concepts.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 navis 加 agere 词族的形式；第二组是相关的行进与引导概念。

entries.definition: Relating to navigation; it must modify a noun such as aid or system, while navigation names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 与导航有关的；必须修饰 aid 或 system 之类名词，而 navigation 命名活动。

entries.definition: Describing water or an aircraft that can be navigated; it judges the route, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可通航的水域或可驾驶的航空器；评判路线，而非动作。

entries.definition: A person who navigates; the -or suffix names the agent, navigation the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 导航的人；-or 后缀命名施动者，navigation 命名活动。

entries.definition: A country's fleet; it comes from navis too, but names the ships as an institution, not the act of steering them.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的舰队；同样来自 navis，但把船只作为建制来命名，而非驾驶动作。

entries.definition: Guiding a vessel through a channel by landmarks; it is one branch of navigation, often close to shore.
entries.definitionCN: 凭地标引导船只通过航道；是导航的一支，常发生在近岸。

entries.definition: Finding one's way through a building or city, often by signs; navigation is broader and includes instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑或城市中认路，常靠标识；navigation 更宽，包含仪器。

entries.definition: Travelling and working at sea; it names a way of life, while navigation names the method.
entries.definitionCN: 在海上旅行与劳作；命名一种生活方式，而 navigation 命名方法。

entries.definition: Choosing the path for data or traffic; it is the technical descendant of route finding.
entries.definitionCN: 为数据或交通选择路径；是找路的技术后裔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: navis 'ship' + agere 'drive' = drive a ship; the same two roots appear in navy and agent.
normal.cn: navis「船」+ agere「驾驶」= 驾船；同两个词根也出现在 navy 与 agent 中。

normal.en: The family runs navigate, navigator, navigational, navigable and navigability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 navigate、navigator、navigational、navigable 与 navigability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: marine navigation, satellite navigation, a navigation system, inland navigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：海上导航、卫星导航、导航系统、内河航运。

normal.en: Navigation answers two questions: where am I, and which way next.
normal.cn: 导航回答两个问题：我在哪里，下一步往哪。

normal.en: Website navigation borrows the sailor's chart: a menu is a map of pages.
normal.cn: 网页导航借用水手的海图：菜单就是页面的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat with no land in sight, correcting its line by a single star.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看不见陆地的小船，靠一颗星修正航线。

abstract.en: Picture a menu bar as a row of harbour lights, each leading to one page.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单栏像一排港口灯，每盏通向一个页面。

abstract.en: Picture a monarch butterfly that has never seen the destination and still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从未见过目的地的帝王蝶，仍然抵达。

examples.en: Satellite navigation has replaced paper charts on many ships.
examples.cn: 卫星导航在许多船上取代了纸质海图。

examples.en: The site's navigation was redesigned so that new users could find the help page.
examples.cn: 网站导航经过重新设计，新用户能找到帮助页面。

examples.en: Inland navigation carries more freight than the nearby roads.
examples.cn: 内河航运运送的货物比附近公路更多。

dict_mnemonic.text: navy（船队）+ action（行动）——驾船找路的行动 → 航行、导航

root: 拉丁 navigatio「航行」← navigare「驾船」= navis（船）+ agere（驾驶）；与 navy、agent 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same loop of fix, compare and correct, but change the traveller: a hull, a walker, a mouse pointer, a butterfly, a spacecraft, an app, a barge and a student of the art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持「定位、比对、修正」的同一循环，只更换行者：船体、行人、鼠标指针、蝴蝶、航天器、应用、驳船，以及学习这门技艺的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: no shore in sight, one bearing checked again and again until the harbour appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见岸，反复校验一个方位，直到港口出现。

branches.en: THE ART: ship-driving as a practice and as a teachable body of knowledge.
branches.cn: 技艺：驾船既是一项实践，也是一套可教授的知识。

branches.en: THE LOOP: fix, compare, correct, whether by star, compass or ground signal.
branches.cn: 循环：定位、比对、修正，不论靠星辰、罗盘还是地面信号。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: menus and satellite systems inherit the same chart and the same lost user.
branches.cn: 新媒介：菜单与卫星系统继承同样的海图与同样会迷路的使用者。

branches.en: WITHOUT INSTRUMENTS: the butterfly answers the two questions with senses only.
branches.cn: 无仪器：蝴蝶只靠感官回答那两个问题。

branches.en: COMMERCE: the old voyage becomes a transport mode measured in tonnage.
branches.cn: 商业：古老的航程变成以吨位计量的运输方式。

intro.en: Navigation is a Latin compound noun: navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive', then -atio. Both roots have large English families of their own.
intro.cn: navigation 是拉丁复合名词：navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」，再加 -atio。两个词根在英语中各自都有大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin navis 'ship' and agere 'drive' form navigare and navigatio; English draws navigate, navigator, navigable, navigational and navy from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 navis「船」与 agere「驾驶」构成 navigare 与 navigatio；英语由此得到 navigate、navigator、navigable、navigational 与 navy。

items.example: Navis is the source of navy and naval.

senses.title: The metric unit of volume
senses.definition: the metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, used for liquids, gases, and loose dry goods
senses.definitionCN: 公制容积单位，等于一立方分米，用于液体、气体以及松散干物
senses.example: The tank holds forty liters of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水箱能装四十升水。
senses.why: The word entered English together with the metric system, which gave volume a decimal unit; a litre is defined as the space inside a cube ten centimetres on each side, so the size is fixed by geometry rather than by any bottle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随公制一起进入英语，公制为容积设定了十进制的单位；一升定义为一个十厘米见方的立方体内部的容积，因此大小由几何确定，而不是由某个瓶子决定。

senses.title: A quantity of that size, especially of a drink or fuel
senses.titleCN: 一升的量：按升卖的一份
senses.definition: a quantity of liquid amounting to one liter, especially as sold or poured
senses.definitionCN: 等于一升的液体量，尤指售卖或倒出的一份
senses.example: He bought a liter of milk on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 他回家路上买了一升牛奶。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can count portions instead of only measuring them; shopkeepers and cooks say a liter of milk the way others say a bottle or a cup, and the unit takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，就可以用来数「份」而不只是测量；店家与厨师说一升牛奶，就像别人说一瓶、一杯，这个单位也就能变复数。

senses.title: A unit for engine displacement
senses.titleCN: 排量：以升计的气缸容积
senses.definition: the same unit used to state the total volume swept by the pistons of an engine, as in a two-liter engine
senses.definitionCN: 同一单位用于表示发动机活塞扫过的总容积，如「两升发动机」
senses.example: The car has a small one-liter engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车配的是一台小型一升发动机。
senses.why: Engine size is itself a volume, so the same unit travels from the kitchen to the garage; a two-liter engine is an engine whose cylinders sweep two liters of air in one cycle.
senses.whyCN: 发动机排量本身就是容积，所以同一单位从厨房走进车库；两升发动机就是气缸在一个循环里扫过两升空气的发动机。

intro.en: Liter came into English through French from a Latin borrowing of a Greek unit name; the American spelling dropped the British re ending.
intro.cn: liter 经法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语对希腊单位名的借用；美式拼写省去了英式的 re 词尾。

items.en: The Greek word litra named a Sicilian unit of weight and, by extension, of capacity; its own earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 litra 指西西里的一种重量单位，也引申指容量单位；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as litra, still a unit of weight, and passed it on to the languages of western Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 litra，仍作重量单位，并把它传进西欧诸语言。

items.en: Old French used litre for a measure of capacity, and French kept the word when the metric system was created.
items.cn: 古法语用 litre 表示一种容量单位，法国在创立公制时保留了这个词。

items.en: English adopted litre along with metric measures in the nineteenth century, spelled in the French way.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪随公制一起引入 litre，并按法语方式拼写。

items.en: American usage settled on liter, while British usage keeps litre; compounds such as milliliter and kiloliter follow the American form in the United States.
items.cn: 美式用法定型为 liter，英式仍作 litre；milliliter、kiloliter 等复合词在美国跟随美式写法。

abstract.en: Decimal measures travel easily because each step is a power of ten, which is why liter fits so neatly with milli- and kilo-.

definition_zh: 先于；在……之前；走在前面；位次高于；作为……的前身
definition_en: to come or go before something or someone in time, order, position, or rank
core_image: 一个人先一步走过路口，后面的人还没到
scene: 颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短的致辞。 A short speech preceded the award ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里 precede 是「在时间上先于」（第 1 个义项）；句意：颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短致辞。场景要点：先后顺序、前一件先发生、后一件才登场；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 先于；在……之前；走在前面；位次高于

senses.title: To happen earlier in time
senses.titleCN: 先于：在时间上更早发生
senses.definition: to happen or exist before something else in time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上比另一事物更早发生或存在
senses.example: A short speech preceded the award ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短致辞。
senses.why: Latin praecedere is prae 'before' plus cedere 'go'. The first sense is simply going earlier along the timeline.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecedere 是 prae“在前”加 cedere“走”。第一个义项就是沿着时间线走得更早。

senses.title: To come earlier in an order
senses.definition: to come before something else in a sequence, list, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在序列、清单或排列中位于另一事物之前
senses.example: The prefix precedes the root in this word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个词里，前缀排在词根之前。
senses.why: Time becomes sequence. What goes first on a line is what has preceded the rest, even when no clock is involved.
senses.whyCN: 时间变成了顺序。在一条线上排在最前的，就是先于其余各项的，即使不涉及钟表。

senses.title: To walk in front of
senses.definition: to go in front of someone, especially in a procession or on a route
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人前面，尤指在游行队伍或行进路线上
senses.example: A drummer preceded the bridal party down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一名鼓手走在迎亲队伍前面，沿街而行。
senses.why: This is the literal picture of the Latin verb: one body moving ahead of another along the same road.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词最字面的画面：一具身体沿着同一条路走在另一具前面。

senses.title: To outrank or take priority
senses.titleCN: 优先：位次或重要性在前
senses.definition: to be higher in rank, importance, or priority than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在级别、重要性或优先次序上高于某人或某物
senses.example: In this court, federal law precedes state law.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个法庭上，联邦法优先于州法。
senses.why: A procession has an order of dignity as well as an order in space. Whoever goes first is served first, so position becomes priority.
senses.whyCN: 队伍不只有空间顺序，还有尊卑顺序。走在前面的人先被招待，于是位置变成了优先权。

senses.title: To go ahead as an introduction
senses.titleCN: 先行开道：把后面的引出来
senses.definition: to come before something as its introduction or preparation
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事物的引子或准备而出现在它之前
senses.example: A period of quiet preceded the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨之前有一段平静。
senses.why: What goes first can prepare the way for what follows. The earlier thing is not merely earlier; it ushers the later one in.
senses.whyCN: 走在前面的东西可以为后面的东西铺路。先前之物不只是更早，它还把后来者引了进来。

senses.title: To be the forerunner of
senses.definition: to be an earlier form or ancestor of something that came later
senses.definitionCN: 是后来某事物的较早形态或前身
senses.example: The telegraph preceded the telephone by decades.
senses.exampleCN: 电报比电话早出现了几十年。
senses.why: Objects too can walk in a line through history. The older device stands in front of the newer one, which is its descendant.
senses.whyCN: 物件也能在历史中排队行走。较老的装置站在较新的前面，后者是它的后裔。

senses.title: To preface with words
senses.titleCN: 开场先说：用话在前面铺一层
senses.definition: to say something before the main statement or text
senses.definitionCN: 在主要陈述或正文之前先说一些话
senses.example: He preceded his refusal with a long apology.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拒绝之前先说了很长一段道歉。
senses.why: Speech has an order too. Words placed in front of the main message are doing the walking-ahead.
senses.whyCN: 言语也有顺序。放在主要信息前面的那些话，承担的就是“走在前面”的功能。

senses.title: Literary: to have gone before others
senses.titleCN: 书面：先走一步（指已故的先辈）
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, to have gone before others, especially to have died earlier
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，指先于他人离去，尤指更早去世
senses.example: We honor those who preceded us and built this town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们敬重那些先我们而去、建起这座小镇的人。
senses.why: A procession through life has a front and a back. Those already further along are described as having preceded the living.
senses.whyCN: 穿越一生的队伍有前有后。已经走得更远的人，就被说成先于在世者而行。

intro.en: Precede is a transparent Latin compound: before plus go. Nearly all of its English senses are versions of that one physical picture.
intro.cn: precede 是一个构造透明的拉丁复合词：“在前”加“走”。它在英语里的几乎每个义项，都是这一幅身体画面的变体。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front of'. It is the source of the English prefix pre-, and it marks position in space as well as priority in time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前、在……之前”。它是英语前缀 pre- 的来源，既标记空间位置，也标记时间上的优先。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, to yield, to withdraw'. English gets cede, accede, exceed, proceed, and succeed from this verb.
items.cn: cedere 意为“走、让、退”。英语的 cede、accede、exceed、proceed、succeed 都出自这个动词。

items.en: Praecedere meant 'to go before, to precede'. It described both people walking ahead and events coming earlier.
items.cn: praecedere 意为“走在前面、先于”。它既描述人走在前头，也描述事件更早发生。

items.en: Old French took the verb as preceder, keeping the sense of going or coming before.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词接作 preceder，保留“走在前面、先来”的意思。

items.en: English precede is recorded in the 15th century. The legal noun precedent and the noun precedence grow from the same root.
items.cn: 英语 precede 记录于 15 世纪。法律名词 precedent 与名词 precedence 都从同一个词根长出。

items.en: Modern usage extends the image to ranks, arguments, inventions, and even the dead: whatever stands earlier in a line has preceded what stands later.
items.cn: 现代用法把这幅画面扩展到等级、论证、发明，甚至逝者：凡在一条线上站得更早的，就先于站得更晚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for going. The second group collects words for coming before in time, order, and rank.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“走”的动词。第二组收表示“在时间、顺序、等级上在前”的词。

entries.definition: to go forward or continue. Pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go', so it moves ahead rather than before.
entries.definitionCN: 前进或继续进行。pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”，所以它是向前走，而非走在前面。

entries.definition: an earlier case used as a rule for later ones. It is the noun of precede in legal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 被用作后来案例规则的先前判例。它是 precede 在法律用法中的名词。

entries.definition: the person who held a post before another. From Latin prae- plus decedere 'to go away', literally one who went before.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人之前担任某职位的人。来自拉丁 prae- 加 decedere“离开”，字面即“先走的人”。

entries.definition: the right to go or be treated first. It is the abstract noun of precede.
entries.definitionCN: 先行或被优先对待的权利。它是 precede 的抽象名词。

entries.definition: to exist or happen before something in date. Predate is narrower, used only of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在日期上早于某事物。predate 更窄，只用于时间。

entries.definition: to be earlier than, or to put an earlier date on. Antedate is formal and often about documents.
entries.definitionCN: 早于，或在文件上写较早的日期。antedate 较正式，常用于文件。

entries.definition: to go in front and show the way. Lead implies guiding; precede only states the order.
entries.definitionCN: 走在前面并带路。lead 含引导之意；precede 只陈述先后顺序。

entries.definition: to have a higher rank than someone. Outrank matches sense 04 exactly and is used of people and offices.
entries.definitionCN: 级别高于某人。outrank 精确对应第 4 义项，多用于人与职位。

entries.definition: to go before as a sign or precursor. Forerun is literary and rare; its noun forerunner is common.
entries.definitionCN: 作为征兆或先驱先行。forerun 带文学色彩且少见；其名词 forerunner 更常用。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the walker ahead, the prefix before the root, the court that hears federal law first, the older machine, and the ancestors.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：走在前面的人、词根前的前缀、先审联邦法的法庭、更老的机器、先辈。

normal.en: Pre- means before, cede means go. Precede is literally before-go.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，cede 是“走”。precede 字面就是“先走”。

normal.en: In the word unhappy, un- precedes happy: it walks in front of the root.
normal.cn: 在 unhappy 这个词里，un- 走在 happy 前面，就是 precede 词根。

normal.en: Take precedence: whoever walks first gets served first.
normal.cn: take precedence：谁走在前面，谁先被招待。

normal.en: The telegraph preceded the telephone; the older machine stands in front of the newer one in history's queue.
normal.cn: 电报先于电话；在历史的队伍里，更老的机器站在更新的前面。

normal.en: Those who preceded us are the ones already further up the road.
normal.cn: 先我们而去的人，就是已经在路上走得更远的那些。

abstract.en: Order is not a thing in the world but a line we draw; precede is the word for standing on the earlier side of that line.
abstract.cn: 顺序不是世界里的物件，而是我们画的线；precede 就是在一条线较早一侧站着的说法。

abstract.en: Priority borrows its grammar from walking: we say law comes first as if laws had legs.
abstract.cn: 优先权借用了行走的语法：我们说法律“在先”，仿佛法律长了腿。

abstract.en: Every forerunner is only recognized as one after the thing it preceded has arrived.
abstract.cn: 每一个前身，都只有在它所先行的那件事到来之后，才被认出来是前身。

examples.en: The years preceding the war were marked by rapid industrial growth.
examples.cn: 战前那些年以快速的工业增长为标志。

examples.en: In the protocol, the chair's remarks precede the vote.
examples.cn: 按议程，主席发言在投票之前。

examples.en: Several small tremors preceded the main earthquake.
examples.cn: 主震之前发生了数次小震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞西德”——普瑞先一步西德而行，就是 precede（先于、走在前面）

root: 拉丁语 praecedere＝prae“在前”+ cedere“走” → 古法语 preceder → 英语 precede（15 世纪）；与 proceed、precedent、predecessor、cede 同根。

sensesIntro.en: One physical image serves everything: something moves ahead of something else on the same line. Time, sequence, space, rank, introduction, ancestry, and even death are all lines along which one item can stand before another.
sensesIntro.cn: 一幅身体画面统摄全部义项：某物在同一条线上走在另一物前面。时间、顺序、空间、等级、引子、前身，甚至死亡，都是可以让一个项目站在另一个之前的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one walker a few steps ahead of another on the same road.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路上，一个行者比另一个领先几步。

branches.en: TIME AND SEQUENCE: earlier on the timeline or in the list.
branches.cn: 时间与顺序：在时间线上或清单里更早。

branches.en: SPACE: a body moving in front along a route.
branches.cn: 空间：一具身体沿路线走在前面。

branches.en: RANK: position turned into priority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：位置变成优先权与位次。

branches.en: INTRODUCTION: what goes first to prepare or frame what follows.
branches.cn: 引子：先走一步，为后面的东西铺路或定框。

branches.en: LINEAGE: the earlier device and the people already further along.
branches.cn: 谱系：更早的器物，以及已经走得更远的人。

intro.en: Precede is built from a prefix of position and a verb of motion. The same two pieces, with other prefixes, produce much of the vocabulary of going and yielding.
intro.cn: precede 由一个表位置的前缀和一个表运动的动词构成。同样两个构件配上别的前缀，产出了大量表示“行走与让渡”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecedere passed into French and English; its participle and noun forms supplied precedent, precedence, and predecessor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecedere 传入法语与英语；它的分词与名词形式提供了 precedent、precedence、predecessor。
